elena-support: Incoming from customer: their app is seeing intermittent 401s and big latency spikes. They say requests are supposed to be routed to us-east but we see some hits to eu-west and a big egress bill. Can infra triage? cc @mike-infra :rotating_light:

mike-infra: On it. Can you paste the failover policy they supplied and an example request-id + time window?

elena-support: Pasting the policy (redacted) they gave us:
```json
{
  "service": "payments-api",
  "failover_policy": [
    {"priority": "1", "region": "us-east-1", "weight": "100"},
    {"priority": "2", "region": "eu-west-1", "weight": "10"}
  ],
  "sticky": true,
  "sticky_key": "session_id",
  "sticky_ttl_seconds": "3600"
}
```
Their request example: req id `req_2026-03-16_09:12:43` window 09:12-09:22 UTC. They also attached a snippet of the API error: `{"error":"invalid_token_region_mismatch","code":401}`

deploy-bot: config-service deployed policy `cfg-commit:8a7f1d` at ts 1921004000 by web-console

jon-ops: Looking at routing traces for that req id. Quick notes: our router reads `failover_policy` array and sorts by `priority` field. The config-service earlier had a change that stopped normalizing number types for policy fields; it left them as strings. The router comparator does a numeric compare but there's a codepath that accidentally falls back to string compare if `Number(value)` is NaN. We have a race where `weight` parse returns NaN for some configs and we end up picking fallback region based on lexicographic sort. Trace below:
```
route_trace: [
  {region: "us-east-1", priority: "1", weight: "100"},
  {region: "eu-west-1", priority: "2", weight: "10"}
]
comparator called: Number(priority) => 1,2 ok; but weight parse: Number("100") => 100, Number("10") => 10; however for some builds Number parsing returned NaN due to stray unicode NBSP in config JSON. comparator fell back to string compare => "eu-west-1" chosen in tie-break path.
```

jon-ops: Repro on staging: curl to us-east returns 401 with body `{"error":"invalid_token_region_mismatch"}` but eu-west returns 200. So requests that should stay in us-east are getting sent to eu-west which has a different auth backend and accepts the token. That's why customer sees random 401s + some successful hits. Also noticed increased cross-region egress in billing for that customer at the same timestamps.

mike-infra: Can you paste the raw curl output?

jon-ops: sure:
```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_XXXXX" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/payments" -H "x-region-prefer: us-east-1"
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"invalid_token_region_mismatch","code":401}

# same token but routed to eu-west by router (trace id attached):
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer tok_XXXXX" "https://eu-west-1.api.redwood.example/v1/payments"
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{"status":"ok","txn_id":"txn_12345"}
```

sarah-ml: I repro'd locally. The config-service accepts numeric-ish strings. The recent change allowed non-ascii whitespace in values from the UI. That NBSP (0xA0) makes Number("100\u00A0") => NaN. Our router fallback uses `priority.toString()` comparison in that path which sorts lexicographically by region id if numeric compare fails. So for some payloads eu-west got prioritized. I can reproduce with this tiny snippet:
```js
const p = ["1", "2"].sort((a,b)=> { const na = Number(a); const nb = Number(b); if (isNaN(na)||isNaN(nb)) return a.localeCompare(b); return na-nb; });
console.log(p);
// inject NBSP into first element and you get reversed order in some edge cases
```

mike-infra: Good catch. Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback config-service to pre-acceptance commit, 2) hotfix router comparator to coerce and trim before compare, 3) update the customer's policy to use proper ints. Which do we want now? Customer is seeing production impact and billing spike.

elena-support: Customer is upset, they said "we are being charged for inter-region traffic and missing transactions". They flagged for SLA breach. Please do rollback if low-risk.

jon-ops: I'll initiate a targeted rollback of the config-service change that relaxed whitespace handling for policy fields. That should stop new bad policies from entering and will restore canonical normalization. Initiating now.

deploy-bot: rollback started: revert `cfg-commit:8a7f1d` -> `cfg-commit:7f3b2c` by automated-rollback at ts 1921005600

mike-infra: After rollback I'm also going to push a patch to the router: trim() all policy fields and coerce to Number with a fallback that errs loudly (reject deployment). Also will add validation in console so weights/priorities must be ints.

jon-ops: Quick notes for postmortem:
- Root cause: config-service allowed non-normalized numeric strings (NBSP) which led to Number() => NaN in router comparator; comparator fallback to string ordering produced unintended region selection.
- Impact: intermittent cross-region routing, 401s when tokens are region-bound, higher egress billing for customer, some latency spikes.
- Mitigation: rollback + patch to comparator + validation in UI + add unit tests and integration test that injects NBSP variants.

elena-support: Customer notified of rollback and mitigation plan, asking for ETA on patch. Can we aim for a patch in next 2 hours? They want credits for the extra egress.

mike-infra: I'll try to get patch out within 90m. Also propose: add a monitor that alerts when cross-region egress for a single customer exceeds baseline by > 50% in 10m window.

sarah-ml: I'll add a tiny fuzz test to our config-parser tests to catch invisible whitespace in numeric fields.

elena-support: thanks team. I'll follow up with the customer once patch is deployed. :thumbsup:

jon-ops: Follow-up action items assigned in tickets: INF-3421 (router coercion), CFG-1987 (console validation), SRE-4302 (egress alert).

mike-infra: marking thread resolved for now; will reopen if we see more noise. :white_check_mark:
